findings.detail: emit_pressure_state returned cycle_snapshot_promoted=false for the 11th consecutive tick. Structural, not intermittent: the promoter keys on the nominal tick (07:00) while Step 4.7 names the file by wall clock (07:02). No wall-clock-named file can ever match a nominal-tick key while the +2 write offset persists.

Nominal 07:00 -> file named 07:02. Eighth consecutive nonzero offset, all +2. The offset is the elapsed time from tick start through drain, staleness, fanout sizing, token claim and the two data fetches; it is a property of the flow, not jitter.

Root cause is ambiguous spec prose, NOT a race or a scan-order effect. .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md Step -1 says: TICK = current UTC time formatted as HH:MM (round to nearest 5-min slot, e.g. 02:05 -> 02:05). That is two contradictory instructions in one line, with a worked example demonstrating no rounding, so the lookup key is whatever reading the consumer lands on that run. Two further defects in the same block: (a) the documented 5-min grid is unsatisfiable, 0 of 35 filenames on disk are 5-min aligned because the writer names by wall clock; (b) a stale note still asserts the snapshot writer is a future task and Step -1 will always miss, which is false, the writer landed and writes every tick. Proposed fix that works under every reading: one unambiguous key, the nominal tick floor(minute/15)*15, computed identically by writer, promoter and consumer, with the consumer taking it from the scheduled_utc token already present in its spawn prompt. Zone .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/ -> agent-father.

c221 HIT cycle-snapshot-07:02.json. Sequence now 06:18 MISS, 06:32 HIT, 06:47 HIT, 07:02 HIT. All four fit exact-read-minute lookup.
